## **1\. INTRODUCTION** {#1.-introduction}

### **1.1 Purpose** {#1.1-purpose}

This Product Requirements Document provides comprehensive specifications for the Masjid App platform. It serves as the authoritative reference for development teams, quality assurance engineers, system architects, product managers, and business stakeholders throughout the project lifecycle.

**Target Audience:**

* Software development teams (backend, frontend, mobile)  
* Quality assurance engineers  
* System architects and technical leads  
* Product managers and project stakeholders

**Document Usage:**  
This document defines what the system does and how users interact with it. All features described are mandatory for initial release unless explicitly marked as future enhancements.

---

### **1.2 Scope** {#1.2-scope}

**In Scope:**

This document covers two primary applications and supporting infrastructure:

**Admin Web Application** enables masjid administrators to:

**Authenticate securely and manage their session**

* Upload annual prayer schedules via CSV or edit manually  
* Create and publish community events  
* Send immediate or scheduled announcements  
* Launch and monitor fundraising campaigns  
* Track donations and view detailed reports  
* Configure masjid profile and settings

**Member Mobile Application** allows community members to:

* View daily prayer times with countdown timers  
* Browse events in calendar and list views  
* Donate to active campaigns via Stripe integration  
* Receive push notifications for announcements and events  
* Configure personalized prayer alerts with athan sounds  
* Use Qibla compass for prayer direction  
* Access complete masjid information

**Backend Services** provide:

* RESTful API layer for data access  
* Database management and persistence  
* File storage for images and media  
* Payment processing integration with Stripe  
* Push notification orchestration via Firebase

---

### **1.3 Definitions** {#1.3-definitions}

**Religious Terms:**

**Masjid:** Islamic place of worship (mosque), encompassing the physical building and community organization.

**Jamah:** Congregation prayer time when prayers are performed collectively at the masjid, typically 10-20 minutes after Athan.

**Athan:** Islamic call to prayer announced before each of the five daily prayers, marking the beginning of the prayer time window.

**Jumu'ah:** Friday congregational prayer that replaces the regular Zuhr (midday) prayer.

**Qibla:** Direction towards the Kaaba in Mecca, which Muslims face during prayer.

**Technical Terms:**

**Single-Tenant Architecture:** Each masjid receives a completely isolated instance of the application, database, and infrastructure.

**Super Admin:** Platform owner responsible for infrastructure management and creating masjid instances.

**Masjid Admin:** Staff member at individual masjid managing content through the admin portal.

**Anonymous User:** Mobile app user accessing the application without registration or authentication.

## **2\. PRODUCT OVERVIEW** {#2.-product-overview}

### **2.1 Product Description** {#2.1-product-description}

The Masjid App modernizes masjid operations and enhances community engagement through two interconnected applications. It addresses critical operational challenges while providing community members with accessible digital services.

**Current Challenges:**

Masjids face significant operational inefficiencies in their daily operations. Administrators manually update prayer times across multiple platforms daily, consuming approximately 15 hours monthly. Community communications fragment across WhatsApp groups, email lists, physical notices, and verbal announcements, resulting in inconsistent message delivery. Fundraising campaigns lack real-time progress visibility, limiting donor confidence and contribution potential. Traditional communication methods increasingly fail to reach younger, digitally-native community members.

**Solution Overview:**

**Admin Web Application (React):**  
 A browser-based management console providing centralized control over masjid operations. Administrators upload annual prayer schedules once via CSV files, create rich media events with speaker details, launch transparent fundraising campaigns, and distribute announcements instantly via push notifications.

**Member Mobile Application (Flutter):**  
 A cross-platform mobile app delivering essential services without requiring user authentication. Community members access automatically updated prayer times with countdown displays, browse events through intuitive interfaces, contribute to campaigns via integrated payment processing, and receive real-time notifications.

**Key Differentiators:**

* **Complete Data Isolation:** Single-tenant architecture ensures each masjid has dedicated infrastructure  
* **Branded Mobile Apps:** Each masjid receives their own App Store/Play Store listing  
* **Anonymous Access:** No user registration required, maximizing accessibility while preserving privacy  
* **Real-Time Sync:** Admin actions immediately reflect in member applications  
* **Professional Payment Processing:** Stripe integration with Apple Pay, Google Pay, and card support

---

### **2.2 Key Features** {#2.2-key-features}

**Prayer Time Management**

Upload annual schedules once via CSV or manage times manually throughout the year. The system supports both Athan (beginning) and Jamah (congregation) times for all six daily prayers, with special handling for multiple Friday Jumu'ah congregations.

Key capabilities:

* Annual CSV upload eliminating daily manual updates  
* Individual prayer time editing for specific dates or ranges  
* Multiple Jumu'ah times for Friday prayers  
* Islamic calendar date conversion  
* Automatic current prayer highlighting with countdown display  
* Instant synchronization to mobile applications

**Event Management**

Create and publish community events with complete details including speaker information, venue specifications, scheduling, and promotional imagery.

Features include:

* Rich event creation with descriptions, speakers, venues, and times  
* Image upload for promotional purposes  
* Draft and publish workflow for review before distribution  
* Event categorization (Educational, Community, Fundraiser, Religious, Youth)  
* Calendar and list view presentations  
* External registration link support  
* Automatic push notifications upon publication  
* Real-time editing with instant mobile sync

**Announcement System**

Broadcast important messages immediately or schedule for future delivery with automatic push notification distribution.

**Capabilities:**

* Immediate announcement broadcasting for urgent communications  
* Scheduled announcements for planned messaging  
* Complete announcement history  
* Push notification integration for high visibility  
* Simple text-based format for quick composition

**Campaign Management**

Launch transparent fundraising campaigns with specific goals, timelines, and real-time progress tracking.

Core features:

* Campaign creation with financial goals and deadlines  
* Category organization (Masjid Development, Education, Charity, Individual Support, General)  
* Real-time donation progress displays  
* Transparent donor recognition (with anonymous option)  
* Complete donation history with payment method tracking  
* Visual progress indicators and percentage displays  
* Campaign end management preserving historical records

**Donation Processing**

Secure payment processing through Stripe Connect supporting multiple payment methods and providing instant receipts.

Payment options:

* Apple Pay integration for iOS devices  
* Google Pay support for Android devices  
* PayPal processing  
* Credit and debit card acceptance  
* Preset donation amounts for quick selection  
* Custom amount entry for specific contributions  
* Anonymous donation option for privacy  
* Processing fee coverage option allowing donors to cover transaction costs  
* Automatic receipt generation and email delivery

**Push Notifications**

Deliver timely information directly to community members through Firebase Cloud Messaging.

Notification types:

* Announcement broadcasts for administrative messages  
* Event publication alerts for new activities  
* Campaign update notifications for fundraising initiatives  
* Topic-based messaging architecture ensuring efficient targeted delivery

**Prayer Alerts**

Personalized prayer reminders with authentic athan sounds scheduled locally on user devices.

Alert features:

* Individual prayer alert configuration (enable/disable per prayer)  
* Multiple adhan audio options (Makkah, Madina, Al Aqsa, Egypt)  
* Local notification scheduling for reliability without network dependency  
* Customizable alert timing preferences

**Masjid Information**

Comprehensive profile displays providing essential contact and facility information.

Information includes:

* Complete contact details (address, phone, email, website)  
* Interactive map integration with navigation capabilities  
* Services listing (marriage ceremonies, hall rental, iftar, counseling, new Muslim support)  
* Facility details (parking, disability access, ablution facilities)  
* Capacity information for men's and women's prayer spaces  
* Expandable about section with masjid history and community information

**Qibla Compass**

Accurate prayer direction finder utilizing device sensors for real-time Qibla calculation.

Functionality:

* Real-time direction calculation using device location and compass  
* Visual Kaaba indicator with degree measurements  
* Dynamic updates as device rotates

### **2.3 User Roles** {#2.3-user-roles}

**Super Admin**

The platform owner responsible for infrastructure management across all masjid instances.

**Primary Responsibilities:**

* Provision AWS infrastructure for new masjid deployments  
* Deploy backend applications and configure databases  
* Create masjid admin user accounts via direct database insertion  
* Configure Stripe Connect and Firebase integrations  
* Build and submit branded mobile apps to app stores  
* Monitor system health and provide technical support

**Access Level:**  
 Unrestricted access to all masjid instances, AWS infrastructure, databases, and administrative functions.

**Technical Requirements:**  
 Advanced expertise in cloud infrastructure, database management, and application deployment.

**User Creation Process (Current):**  
 Manually inserts admin users into the database with hashed passwords. Future enhancement will provide API-based user management.

---

**Masjid Admin**

Staff members at individual masjids manage daily operations through the web portal.

**Core Responsibilities:**

* Upload and maintain accurate prayer schedules  
* Create and publish community events with full details  
* Compose and distribute announcements to community  
* Launch and monitor fundraising campaigns  
* Track donation activity and view reports  
* Update masjid profile and contact information

**Access Restrictions:**

* Limited to their specific masjid instance only  
* Cannot access other masjid data or system configurations  
* Cannot reset own password (must contact Super Admin)  
* Read-only access to donation records (cannot modify financial transactions)

**Technical Proficiency:**  
 Moderate skills required, comfortable with web browsers and basic file management.

**Account Management:**  
 Accounts created manually by Super Admin. No self-service password reset currently available.

---

**Mobile App Member**

Community members accessing masjid services through the mobile application without any authentication.

**Available Capabilities:**

* View prayer times with real-time countdown displays  
* Browse events in calendar and list formats  
* Make donations to active campaigns  
* Receive push notifications for announcements and events  
* Configure personalized prayer alerts  
* Access Qibla direction compass  
* View complete masjid information

**Privacy Characteristics:**

* No registration or login required  
* Zero personal data collection during normal use  
* Settings stored locally on device only (not synced to server)  
* Anonymous donation option available  
* Fresh install requires reconfiguring all preferences

**Data Storage:**

* Prayer times cached for 30 days for offline access  
* User preferences saved locally using device storage  
* No cross-device synchronization  
* Donation history not stored in application (receipts via email only)

## **3\. TECHNOLOGY STACK** {#3.-technology-stack}

### **3.1 Backend Technology** {#3.1-backend-technology}

The backend is built on Spring Boot 3.2 running Java 21, providing enterprise-grade stability and performance.

**Core Framework:**

* Spring Boot 3.2.x (Java 21 LTS)  
* Maven 3.9 for dependency management  
* AWS Elastic Beanstalk for deployment

---

### **3.2 Admin Web Application** {#3.2-admin-web-application}

Built with React 18 and styled using TailwindCSS for rapid, responsive development.

**Core Technologies:**

* React 18.x for component-based UI  
* TailwindCSS 3.x for utility-first styling  
* Vite 5.x as build tool  
* npm for package management

**State Management:**  
 React Context API (built-in, no external dependencies)

**Browser Compatibility:**  
 Chrome 90+, Firefox 88+, Safari 14+, Microsoft Edge 90+

---

### 

### **3.3 Member Mobile Application** {#3.3-member-mobile-application}

Developed using Flutter 3.16 enabling single codebase deployment to iOS and Android.

**Core Framework:**

* Flutter 3.16.x (Dart 3.2)  
* Riverpod 2.4.x for state management

**Platform Support:**

* iOS 14.0 and above  
* Android API 26+ (Android 8.0+)

**Build Configuration:**  
 Flutter flavors enable per-masjid branding from single codebase

---

### **3.4 Infrastructure** {#3.4-infrastructure}

All infrastructure deployed on Amazon Web Services (AWS) using single-tenant architecture.

**Core AWS Services:**

| Service | Configuration | Purpose |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| Elastic Beanstalk | Java 21 platform, t3.medium | Backend application hosting |
| RDS PostgreSQL | PostgreSQL 15, db.t3.medium, 100GB | Database management |
| S3 | Standard storage class | Media file storage |
| CloudWatch | 30-day log retention | Logging and monitoring |
| Route 53 | Hosted zones per masjid | DNS management |
| Certificate Manager | Auto-renewal enabled | SSL/TLS certificates |

**Third-Party Services:**

* **Stripe Connect:** Payment processing with separate accounts per masjid  
* **Firebase Cloud Messaging:** Push notification delivery to mobile devices  
* **Deployment Model:**  
   Each masjid receives dedicated instances of all infrastructure components, ensuring complete data isolation and independent scaling.

---

 

## **4\. ADMIN WEB APPLICATION** {#4.-admin-web-application}

### **4.1 LOGIN** {#4.1-login}

**Purpose:**  
 Authenticate masjid administrators and establish secure sessions for accessing the admin portal.

**![][image1]**  
 *Description: Login page showing username field, password field with visibility toggle, green "Log In" button, and footer with Terms and Privacy Policy links*

---

**Screen Components:**

The login screen presents a clean, centered authentication interface. The username field accepts alphanumeric input with a minimum of 3 characters, displayed with a user icon on the right. The password field masks input by default, showing dots for entered characters, with an eye icon allowing temporary visibility toggle. The Log In button remains disabled until both fields contain valid input, then enables with green styling. Footer links provide access to Terms of Use and Privacy Policy documents.

**User Workflow:**

1. **Access Portal:** User navigates to their masjid-specific admin URL  
2. **Enter Credentials:** Input username and password provided by Super Admin  
3. **Toggle Password Visibility:** Optional \- click eye icon to verify password entry  
4. **Submit Authentication:** Click enabled Log In button  
5. **System Validation:** Backend verifies credentials against hashed database records  
6. **Successful Login:** User redirected to Dashboard with valid 24-hour session token  
7. **Error Handling:** Invalid credentials or inactive accounts display appropriate error messages

**Session Management:**

Authentication generates a JWT token valid for 24 hours, stored in browser localStorage. The token accompanies all subsequent API requests in the Authorization header. Sessions expire automatically after 24 hours, requiring new login. No automatic refresh mechanism exists in the current implementation.

**Security Measures:**

* All communication occurs over HTTPS with TLS encryption  
* Passwords hashed using bcrypt before storage (never stored as plain text)  
* Rate limiting restricts login attempts to 10 per 15 minutes per IP address  
* Account lockout triggers after 5 consecutive failed attempts for 30 minutes  
* No concurrent session management (new login invalidates previous token)

**Error Messages:**

* Invalid credentials: "Invalid username or password"  
* Inactive account: "Your account has been deactivated. Contact support."  
* Network failure: "Unable to connect. Please check your internet."  
* Server error: "Something went wrong. Please try again later."

### **4.2 DASHBOARD** {#4.2-dashboard}

**Purpose:**  
 Provide centralized overview of current masjid operations including today's prayer times, upcoming events, and active fundraising campaigns.

**![][image2]**  
 *Description: Dashboard showing navigation header, dual-calendar date display, six prayer time cards with current prayer highlighted in green, four quick action buttons, upcoming events section, and active campaigns with progress bars*

---

**Screen Layout:**

**Header Navigation:**  
 The top navigation bar contains the masjid logo linking to dashboard, main menu items (Dashboard, Prayer Management, Events & Announcements, Campaign, App Settings), notification bell icon for future alerts, and profile dropdown providing access to My Profile and Logout options.

**Date Display:**  
 A prominent banner displays both Gregorian and Islamic calendar dates (example: "Thursday, October 7, 2025" and "15 Rabi-Al-Thani 1447"). Left and right arrow buttons enable viewing prayer times for adjacent days, with range limited to ±365 days from current date.

**Prayer Times Cards:**  
 Six cards arranged horizontally display Fajr, Sunrise, Zuhr (or Jumu'ah on Fridays), Asr, Maghrib, and Isha prayers. Each card shows the prayer name in uppercase, large Jamah (congregation) time, and smaller Athan time below. The current prayer receives green background highlighting based on time-based calculation, while other prayers display with light grey backgrounds.

**Quick Action Buttons:**  
 Four white buttons with grey borders provide shortcuts to common tasks:

* Add Event (opens modal dialog)  
* Add Announcement (opens modal dialog)  
* Create Campaign (opens modal dialog)  
* Update Prayer Timings (navigates to prayer management page)

**Upcoming Events:**  
 This section displays the next 2 chronologically ordered events with title, category badge, truncated description, speaker name, date, and time. Clicking any event card navigates to full event details. Empty state displays: "No upcoming events. Create your first event\!"

**Active Campaigns:**  
 Shows up to 3 active fundraising campaigns sorted by end date (soonest first). Each campaign card displays title, category label, visual progress bar, percentage complete, goal amount, raised amount, end date, and active status badge. Clicking campaigns navigates to detailed donation history. Empty state displays: "No active campaigns. Launch your first fundraiser\!"

**Data Workflow:**

On page load, the dashboard sends three parallel API requests to retrieve current prayer times, upcoming events (limit 2), and active campaigns (limit 3). The backend calculates the current prayer based on server time, determining which prayer's Jamah time has passed but the next prayer hasn't arrived. The frontend displays all data with automatic refresh every 5 minutes to maintain currency during extended sessions.

**User Interactions:**

* **Date Navigation:** Click arrows to view previous/next day prayer times  
* **Quick Actions:** Click any button to immediately access common tasks  
* **View Events:** Click event cards for complete details  
* **Monitor Campaigns:** Click campaign cards to see donation history and progress  
* **Profile Access:** Click dropdown to view profile or logout  
* **Manual Refresh:** Use refresh icon to immediately update all dashboard data

---

### **4.3 PRAYER TIME MANAGEMENT** {#4.3-prayer-time-management}

**Purpose:**  
 Manage annual prayer schedules through CSV upload or manual editing with support for multiple Jumu'ah times.

#### **Prayer Timetable View** {#prayer-timetable-view}

**![][image3]**  
 *Description: Monthly calendar view displaying prayer times in table format with columns for each prayer, rows for each day showing Begins and Jamah times, navigation arrows, CSV Upload button, and Update Prayer Time button*

---

**Screen Components:**

The timetable displays a monthly calendar view with current month and Islamic month range at the top. Navigation arrows allow movement between months. Two primary action buttons provide access to CSV Upload and Update Prayer Time functions.

The prayer table contains columns for Day, Hijri Date, Fajr, Sunrise, Zuhr, Asr, Maghrib, and Isha. Each day shows two rows: "Begins" displaying Athan times and "Jamah" showing congregation times. The current day receives highlighting for easy identification. The table scrolls vertically to accommodate all month days.

**User Actions:**

* **View Schedule:** Browse complete monthly prayer times  
* **Navigate Months:** Use arrows to view different months  
* **Upload CSV:** Access bulk upload functionality for annual schedules  
* **Manual Edit:** Open editor to modify specific dates or ranges

---

#### **CSV Upload** {#csv-upload}

**Purpose:**  
 Enable efficient annual prayer schedule upload through structured CSV file import.

**Upload Process:**

1. **Initiate Upload:** Click CSV Upload button to open modal  
2. **Select File:** Choose properly formatted CSV file from local system  
3. **File Validation:** System checks file format, column structure, date formats, and time formats  
4. **Processing:** Backend parses CSV and imports prayer times to database  
5. **Success Confirmation:** Modal displays success message with count of imported records  
6. **Mobile Sync:** Prayer times immediately available in mobile application  
7. **Error Handling:** Specific validation errors display with line numbers for correction

**CSV Format Requirements:** \[To be defined in Section 7.1\]

**Validation Rules:**

The system validates that all required columns are present, dates follow consistent format patterns, times use valid 12/24-hour notation, no duplicate dates exist, and all prayer times for each day are complete. Any validation failures prevent import and display specific error messages indicating the problem row and field.

---

#### **Manual Prayer Time Edit** {#manual-prayer-time-edit}

**![][image4]**  
 *Description: Full-screen modal showing date range selector, tabbed interface for Daily Prayers and Jumu'ah, time input fields for each prayer showing both Athan and Jamah times, Save and Cancel buttons*

---

**Purpose:**  
 Provide granular control for editing prayer times for specific dates or date ranges.

**Edit Workflow:**

1. **Open Editor:** Click Update Prayer Time button  
2. **Select Date Range:** Choose start and end dates using calendar picker  
3. **Edit Daily Prayers Tab:**  
   * Set Fajr Athan and Jamah times  
   * Set Sunrise time (informational, no Jamah)  
   * Set Zuhr Athan and Jamah times  
   * Set Asr Athan and Jamah times  
   * Set Maghrib Athan and Jamah times  
   * Set Isha Athan and Jamah times  
4. **Edit Jumu'ah Tab:**  
   * Set first Jumu'ah time  
   * Optionally add second Jumu'ah time using "+" button  
   * Remove additional Jumu'ah times if needed  
5. **Save Changes:** Submit updates to backend  
6. **Confirmation:** Success message confirms update  
7. **Immediate Sync:** Changes reflect instantly in mobile application

**Date Range Functionality:**

Users can edit a single day by selecting the same date for both start and end, or modify extended periods by selecting different dates. The system applies identical time changes to all days in the selected range, useful for daylight savings adjustments or seasonal variations.

**Jumu'ah Management:**

The dedicated Jumu'ah tab allows configuration of multiple Friday prayer times. Many larger masjids conduct two or three separate Jumu'ah congregations to accommodate attendance. Users add additional times using the plus button and remove them using delete icons. These times replace the regular Zuhr prayer on Fridays in the mobile display.

---

### **4.4 EVENTS MANAGEMENT** {#4.4-events-management}

**Purpose:**  
 Create, organize, and publish community events with complete details and promotional content.

---

#### **Events List View** {#events-list-view}

**![][image5]**  
 *Description: Events list interface with filter tabs (All, Upcoming, Past, Drafts), search bar, New Event button, List/Calendar view toggle, and table displaying event title, date/time, message preview, type, status, and action icons*

The events list provides comprehensive event management through filtered views and search capability. Filter tabs at the top allow quick switching between all events, upcoming events only, past events, and draft events. A search field enables finding specific events by title or keyword. The New Event button opens the creation modal. A toggle button switches between list and calendar views.

The events table displays key information in columns: Title, Date & Time, Message (description preview), Type (category), Status (Sent/Draft/Scheduled), and Action icons. Each row represents one event with View and Edit icons for quick access.

**User Operations:**

* **Filter Events:** Click tabs to show All, Upcoming, Past, or Draft events only  
* **Search Events:** Type in search field to find events by title or content  
* **Create Event:** Click New Event to open creation modal  
* **View Details:** Click view icon to see complete event information  
* **Edit Event:** Click edit icon to modify event details  
* **Toggle View:** Switch between list and calendar presentations

#### **Events Calendar View** {#events-calendar-view}

**![][image6]**  
 *Description: Monthly calendar grid with dates, colored dots indicating events on specific days, month navigation arrows, and view toggle*

---

**Purpose:**  
 Visualize event distribution across the month for easier scheduling and conflict identification.

**Calendar Features:**

The monthly calendar displays a standard grid with one cell per day. Days containing events show colored indicator dots below the date number. Multiple events on a single day display multiple dots. The current date receives distinct highlighting. Navigation arrows allow moving between months. Clicking any date filters the event list below to show only that day's events.

**Interaction Model:**

* **Navigate Months:** Use arrow buttons to change displayed month  
* **Identify Event Days:** Quickly see which dates have scheduled events  
* **View Day Events:** Click any date to see that day's events in list below

#### **Add New Campaign** {#add-new-campaign}

---

**Purpose:**  
 Launch new fundraising initiatives with clear goals and compelling descriptions.

**Form Fields:**

**Title (Required):**

**Cause (Required):**  
 Dropdown selection from categories:

* Masjid Development  
* Education & Dawah  
* Charity & Welfare

**Target Amount (Required):**  
 Currency input for fundraising goal (Example: £15,000). System displays with proper currency formatting.

**Start & End Date (Required):**  
 Date range picker defining campaign active period.

**Description (Required):**  
 Detailed explanation of campaign purpose, fund usage, and community impact.

**Upload Image (Optional):**  
 Campaign banner image displayed in mobile app cards and details.

**Campaign Creation Workflow:**

1. **Open Campaign Form:** Click Create Campaign from dashboard or campaigns page  
2. **Enter Basic Information:** Fill title, select cause category  
3. **Set Financial Goal:** Input target amount in pounds  
4. **Define Timeline:** Select start and end dates  
5. **Write Description:** Compose compelling campaign story explaining purpose and impact  
6. **Upload Image:** Add visual appeal with relevant imagery  
7. **Choose Action:**  
   * Save as Draft: Stores campaign without publishing  
   * Create Campaign: Publishes immediately to mobile app  
8. **Confirmation:** Success message displays with campaign ID  
9. **Mobile Availability:** Published campaigns appear instantly in app

**Validation Rules:**

* Target amount must be positive number greater than zero  
* End date must be after start date  
* Start date can be today or future date  
* Description minimum 50 characters for meaningful context  
* Image file size limited to \[SIZE TO BE DEFINED\]

**Note to Admins:**  
 Message displays: "When you publish, the campaign goes live in the Mobile App and users can start donating immediately."

#### **Campaign Details** {#campaign-details}

**![][image13]**  
 *Description: Campaign overview showing header with title and category, progress metrics with visual progress bar, goal/raised amounts, date range, Edit and End Campaign buttons, and donation history table with columns for Name, Amount, Date, Payment Method, Status*

**Purpose:**  
 Monitor campaign performance and view complete donation history with transparency.

**Display Sections:**

**Campaign Header:**  
 Displays campaign title, category badge, status indicator (Active/Ended), and full description text.

**Progress Metrics:**  
 Visual progress bar shows percentage toward goal with colored fill. Large numbers display goal amount (e.g., £15,000), current raised amount (e.g., £10,500), and calculated percentage (e.g., 70%). Start and end dates provide timeline context.

**Action Buttons:**

* Edit Campaign: Opens edit modal for modifying details  
* End Campaign: Triggers confirmation dialog to close campaign

**Donation History Table:**

| Column | Content |
| ----- | ----- |
| Name | Donor name or "Anonymous" if privacy selected |
| Amount | Contribution amount with currency symbol |
| Date | Transaction date and time |
| Payment Method | PayPal, Stripe, Apple Pay, Google Pay, or Card |
| Status | Successful, Failed, or Processing |

The table displays all donations chronologically (newest first) with pagination for campaigns receiving many contributions. Each row represents one transaction as recorded by Stripe.

**Real-Time Updates:**

Campaign details refresh automatically every 30 seconds when the page opens. New donations trigger immediate updates to the raised amount, progress percentage, and donation table. Progress bar animates to a new percentage level. All connected admin sessions see synchronized data.

**User Actions:**

* **Monitor Progress:** Track campaign performance toward goal  
* **Review Donations:** See individual contributions and payment methods  
* **Identify Donors:** View supporter names (respecting anonymous preferences)  
* **Edit Campaign:** Modify description, dates, or image  
* **End Campaign:** Close campaign when goal reached or deadline passed

---

#### **Edit Campaign** {#edit-campaign}

**![][image14]**  
 *Description: Same form as Add Campaign but pre-populated with existing data and Update button*

---

**Purpose:**  
 Modify active campaign details while preserving donation history.

**Editable Fields:**

* Campaign title  
* Category/cause  
* Description  
* End date (can only extend, not shorten)  
* Campaign image

**Restricted Fields:**

* Target amount cannot change once donations received  
* Start date cannot change after campaign begins  
* Existing donations remain unaffected by edits

**Update Process:**

1. **Select Campaign:** Click Edit Campaign button from details view  
2. **Review Current Data:** Form displays all existing information  
3. **Modify Allowed Fields:** Change description, extend end date, update image  
4. **Save Changes:** Click Update button  
5. **Validation:** System prevents invalid modifications  
6. **Confirmation:** Success message confirms update  
7. **Mobile Sync:** Changes reflect immediately in app

**Business Logic:**

Preventing target amount changes after donations received maintains campaign integrity and donor trust. Donations made toward specific goals should not have goals retroactively changed. If significantly more funds needed, create new campaign with updated goal rather than modifying existing campaign.

---

#### **End Campaign** {#end-campaign}

**![][image15]**  
 *Description: Confirmation dialog with warning message, explanation of consequences, Cancel and Yes buttons*

---

**Purpose:**  
 Formally close campaigns and remove from active mobile app display while preserving records.

**Confirmation Dialog:**

**Warning Message:**  
 "Are you sure you want to end this campaign?"

**Consequences Explained:**

* Campaign will no longer appear in mobile app campaigns list  
* No new donations can be made  
* Donation history remains permanently accessible in admin portal  
* Campaign status changes to "Ended"  
* Action cannot be undone

**Action Buttons:**

* Cancel (gray): Abort ending process, return to campaign details  
* Yes (red): Confirm campaign closure

**End Campaign Workflow:**

1. **Initiate Ending:** Click End Campaign button on details page  
2. **Review Confirmation:** Read consequences carefully  
3. **Confirm or Cancel:**  
   * Cancel: Returns to campaign details with no changes  
   * Yes: Proceeds with ending  
4. **Status Update:** Campaign status changes to "Ended"  
5. **Mobile Removal:** Campaign disappears from app immediately  
6. **History Preservation:** All donation records remain in admin portal  
7. **No Reactivation:** Ended campaigns cannot be reopened

**Post-End State:**

Ended campaigns remain accessible in the admin portal under Past or All campaigns filter. Donation history stays fully viewable for financial reconciliation and reporting. Campaign details remain editable for record-keeping purposes (updating descriptions or categorization). To continue fundraising for the same purpose, create a new campaign referencing previous efforts.

**When to End Campaigns:**

* Goal amount successfully reached  
* End date arrived  
* Masjid decides to stop accepting donations for specific initiative  
* Campaign replaced by new campaign with updated goals

## **5\. MEMBER MOBILE APPLICATION** {#5.-member-mobile-application}

### **5.1 HOME \- PRAYER TIMES** {#5.1-home---prayer-times}

**Purpose:**  
 Display today's prayer schedule with real-time countdown to next prayer, serving as the primary landing screen for daily masjid interaction.

---

#### **Regular Day View** {#regular-day-view}

**![][image18]**

 *Description: Prayer times home screen showing masjid banner image at top, masjid name and address, dual-calendar date display, large circular countdown timer in center showing "Asr in HH:MM:SS", prayer times table with Adhan and Jamah columns for six prayers with current prayer highlighted in green, Previous/Today/Next Day navigation buttons at bottom, and bottom tab bar with Home, Calendar, Donate, Notifications, Profile icons*

**Screen Components:**

**Header Section:**  
 The screen opens with a prominent banner image of the masjid building creating visual identity and connection. Beneath the image, the masjid name appears in bold text (e.g., "NWKMA \- Masjid Abu Bakar") followed by the complete street address. A small notification bell icon in the upper right provides access to the notifications screen.

**Date Display:**  
 Dual-calendar format shows both Gregorian (left side, e.g., "Thu, 7 October 2025") and Islamic (right side, e.g., "15 Rabi-Al-Thani 1447") dates prominently below the header, maintaining cultural and religious relevance.

**Countdown Timer:**  
 The centerpiece features a large circular progress indicator with an arc showing time progression toward the next prayer. The center displays which prayer is approaching (e.g., "Asr in") with the remaining time in hours, minutes, and seconds (HH:MM:SS format). The arc fills gradually as time passes, providing visual countdown representation.

**Prayer Times Table:**  
 A clean table presents all six prayers with two columns:

* **Adhan Column:** Shows when prayer time begins  
* **Jamah Column:** Shows congregation prayer time

The six rows display:

1. Fajr (with Adhan and Jamah times)  
2. Sunrise (Adhan time only, no Jamah as it's informational)  
3. Zuhr (with Adhan and Jamah times)  
4. Asr (highlighted in green if current prayer)  
5. Maghrib (with Adhan and Jamah times)  
6. Isha (with Adhan and Jamah times)

The current prayer row receives green background highlighting based on real-time calculation.

**Navigation Controls:**  
 Three buttons below the prayer table enable date navigation:

* Previous (left): View yesterday's prayer times  
* Today (center): Return to current date  
* Next Day (right): View tomorrow's prayer times

**Bottom Tab Bar:**  
 Fixed navigation bar with five icons:

* Home (green, currently active)  
* Calendar  
* Donate (center, elevated green circle for prominence)  
* Notifications  
* Profile

**User Interactions:**

The screen automatically loads today's prayer times when opened, displaying cached data if offline or fetching fresh data if connected. The countdown timer updates every second, showing precise time remaining until next prayer. The current prayer highlighting updates automatically when prayer times pass. Users can swipe left or right to change dates, or tap navigation buttons. Tapping the Today button instantly returns the current date from any other date. The bell icon opens the notifications screen. Bottom tab icons navigate to respective application sections.

**Offline Functionality:**

Prayer times cache locally for 30 days (15 days past, 15 days future), enabling full functionality without internet connection. The countdown timer continues updating using the device clock. Cached data refreshes automatically when connection restores. Users see a subtle indicator if viewing cached data instead of live data.

**Current Prayer Logic:**

The system determines current prayer by comparing device time against prayer schedule. The prayer whose Jamah time has passed but the next prayer's Jamah time hasn't arrived yet is considered current. For example, if the time is 2:45 PM and Zuhr Jamah was 1:30 PM while Asr Jamah is 4:25 PM, Zuhr is highlighted as current. After Isha until Fajr Athan next morning, Isha remains highlighted. The countdown always displays time remaining to the next prayer's Jamah time, not Athan time.

---

#### 

#### 

#### 

#### **Friday (Jumu'ah) View** {#friday-(jumu'ah)-view}

**![][image19]**  
 *Description: Identical layout to regular day but third prayer row shows "Jumu'ah" instead of "Zuhr" with appropriate congregation time*

---

**Friday-Specific Behavior:**

Every Friday, the system automatically detects the day and replaces the Zuhr prayer row with Jumu'ah. The label changes from "Zuhr" to "Jumu'ah" while maintaining the same two-column format showing Athan (if configured) and Jamah times. This happens automatically without user intervention based on date detection.

The Jumu'ah row displays identical styling to other prayers, with green highlighting if it's the current prayer time. The countdown timer references Jumu'ah instead of Zuhr when calculating time remaining. All other prayers (Fajr, Sunrise, Asr, Maghrib, Isha) remain unchanged.

Users see no visual difference in interface beyond the prayer name change, maintaining consistency in user experience. Historical Friday dates also display Jumu'ah when viewing past days, and future Fridays show Jumu'ah when browsing ahead.

---

#### **Multiple Jumu'ah View** {#multiple-jumu'ah-view}

**Multiple Congregation Support:**

For masjids conducting multiple Friday prayer congregations to accommodate large attendance, the system displays multiple Jumu'ah rows. The first row shows "Jumu'ah 1" with its Athan (if applicable) and Jamah time. The second row shows "Jumu'ah 2" with its congregation time. Each congregation maintains separate timing allowing users to choose which service to attend.

The display clearly differentiates between congregations through numbering (Jumu'ah 1, Jumu'ah 2). If a third congregation exists, it displays as Jumu'ah 3\. The countdown timer calculates time to the nearest upcoming Jumu'ah congregation, switching to the next congregation once the first has passed.

Green highlighting applies to whichever Jumu'ah congregation is currently in progress based on time calculations. This helps users identify which service is happening now versus upcoming services.

---

### **5.2 CALENDAR** {#5.2-calendar}

**Purpose:**  
 Provide comprehensive monthly prayer timetables and event schedules through tabbed interface with calendar and list presentations.

---

#### **Prayer Time Tab** {#prayer-time-tab}

**![][image20]**  
 *Description: Tab selector showing "Prayer Time" active and "Events" inactive, month/year header with Islamic month range, navigation arrows, scrollable table with columns for Day, Hijri Date, Fajr, Sunrise, Zuhr, Asr, Maghrib, Isha, each day showing Begins and Jamah times, current day row highlighted*

---

**Screen Organization:**

The screen begins with a tab selector offering two options: Prayer Time (currently active) and Events. The month and year display prominently (e.g., "Jan 2026") with the corresponding Islamic month range beneath (e.g., "Rabi-Al-Thani, 1447 \- Jumada-Al-Awal, 1447"). Left and right arrow buttons enable navigation between months.

**Prayer Timetable Structure:**

The main content presents a comprehensive table with the following columns:

* Day (date number and day name abbreviation)  
* Hijri (Islamic calendar date)  
* Fajr, Sunrise, Zuhr, Asr, Maghrib, Isha (each prayer with two rows)

Each day occupies two rows in the table:

1. **Begins:** Shows Athan times for each prayer  
2. **Jamah:** Shows congregation times for each prayer

The table scrolls vertically to accommodate all month days. The current day's row receives distinct highlighting (green background or border) for easy identification.

**User Interactions:**

Users browse the complete monthly schedule by scrolling through the table. Navigation arrows allow moving to previous or future months to plan ahead or review historical schedules. Tapping any prayer time has no action (read-only display). The tab selector enables switching to Events view. All data loads from local cache if available, fetching from server only when cache expires or user manually refreshes.

**Data Currency:**

Prayer times update whenever the admin uploads new CSV data or makes manual edits. The mobile app checks for updates during app launch and periodically in the background. Users can pull-to-refresh for immediate update checking. The Islamic dates are calculated automatically based on Gregorian dates using the configured conversion method.

---

#### 

#### 

#### 

#### 

#### **Events Tab \- Calendar View** {#events-tab---calendar-view}

*`![][image21]`*  
 *Description: Monthly calendar grid (7x5 or 7x6) with day names header, dates in cells, colored dots below dates indicating events, current date in green circle, selected date highlighted, list of that day's events below calendar showing event cards with time, title, description preview*

---

**Calendar Grid Display:**

The monthly calendar presents in standard grid format with Sunday through Saturday columns. Each date cell shows the day number with event indicator dots below numbers for dates containing events. Multiple events on one date show multiple dots (up to 3 dots visible, with "+N" text if more than 3 events exist).

The current date displays in a green circle. When users tap a date, it receives selection highlighting (different from current date indicator). The calendar includes dates from the previous/next month in gray to complete weeks, though these typically don't show events.

**Event List Below Calendar:**

Beneath the calendar grid, a date header shows the selected date in full format (e.g., "Thursday, 02 Jan, 2026"). If the selected date is today, a "Today" button appears allowing quick return to the current date.

Event cards for the selected date display chronologically, each showing:

* Time range (e.g., "07:00 PM \- 08:30 PM")  
* Event title in bold  
* Description preview (truncated to approximately 2 lines)  
* Registration link button if external registration available

**User Interactions:**

Users navigate months using arrow buttons at the top. Tapping any date selects it and displays that day's events below. Tapping event cards opens the full event details modal. The view toggle button (list/calendar icons) switches to chronological list view. Pull-to-refresh updates event data from server.

**Empty States:**

Dates without events show no indicator dots. Selecting a date with no events displays a message: "No events scheduled for this date."

---

#### 

#### 

#### 

#### **Events Tab \- List View** {#events-tab---list-view}

**![][image22]**  
 *Description: Chronological list of events with date headers (formatted as "15 Mon"), event cards showing title, time range, color-coded left border, expanding downward through upcoming events*

---

**List Presentation:**

Events display in chronological order from nearest to furthest future date. Date headers separate events by day, showing day number and abbreviated day name (e.g., "15 Mon"). Small dot markers appear next to date headers indicating event presence.

Each event card contains:

* Event title (bold, prominent)  
* Time range (smaller text below title)  
* Color-coded left border indicating event category or status

The list scrolls vertically through all upcoming events. Past events can be hidden or shown based on filter settings. The interface provides visual timeline representation through consistent date headers and card styling.

**User Interactions:**

Users scroll through the complete event list to browse all upcoming activities. Tapping any event card opens the full event details modal with complete information. The view toggle switches back to the calendar grid. Pull-to-refresh updates event data. Infinite scroll loads more events as users approach the list bottom.

**Advantages Over Calendar View:**

List view better accommodates browsing many events without repeatedly selecting different dates. Users see all upcoming events in a single scroll, useful for planning attendance across multiple weeks. The chronological presentation makes temporal relationships between events clearer.

### **5.3 CAMPAIGNS AND DONATIONS** {#5.3-campaigns-and-donations}

**Purpose:**  
 Enable community members to discover active fundraising campaigns and make secure donations through integrated payment processing.

---

#### **Campaign List** {#campaign-list}

**![][image23]**  
 *Description: Screen showing category header, campaign cards with category icon, title, goal amount in large text, category badge, description preview, horizontal progress bar showing visual completion percentage, raised amount text, "Ongoing" status badge, share icon, and prominent green "Donate Now" button*

**Screen Structure:**

Campaigns are organized by category with category headers separating different causes (e.g., "Education & Dawah", "Masjid Development"). Each campaign displays as a distinct card with comprehensive information.

**Campaign Card Components:**

**Visual Elements:**

* Category icon at top (representing cause type)  
* Campaign title in bold, large text  
* Goal amount prominently displayed (e.g., "£15,000")  
* Category badge label  
* Share icon for social sharing

**Content Elements:**

* Brief description (truncated to approximately 3-4 lines)  
* Full description visible after tapping card

**Progress Indicators:**

* Horizontal progress bar with colored fill showing percentage toward goal  
* Raised amount text (e.g., "£10,500 raised")  
* Status badge ("Ongoing" in green, "Ended" in gray)

**Action Button:**

* Large green "Donate Now" button spanning card width

**User Interactions:**

Users scroll vertically through all active campaigns organized by category. Tapping anywhere on the card (except specific buttons) opens the full campaign details screen. The share icon triggers native share sheets allowing users to send campaign links via messaging apps, social media, or email. The "Donate Now" button immediately navigates to the donation amount selection screen for quick contributions.

**Real-Time Updates:**

Progress bars and raised amounts update in real-time as donations occur. When users return to campaigns list after donating, they immediately see their contribution reflected in updated totals. Campaign cards automatically remove from the list when admins end campaigns, with smooth animation.

#### **Payment Details** {#payment-details}

**![][image26]**  
 *Description: Payment configuration screen showing two checkboxes ("Donate as anonymous" and "Cover processing fees with £X.XX addition"), total amount in large text aligned right, three payment method buttons (Apple Pay in black, PayPal with logo, "Pay With Card" in white)*

---

**Payment Configuration Options:**

**Anonymous Donation Checkbox:**  
 Checkbox with label: "Donate as anonymous"

When checked, the donor's name will not appear in the public recent donations list visible in the mobile app. The donation still processes normally with a name submitted to Stripe for receipt purposes, but the admin portal and mobile app display "Anonymous" instead of the donor name. This option respects donor privacy preferences while maintaining transaction integrity.

**Processing Fee Coverage Checkbox:**  
 Checkbox with label: "I want to make an additional donation to cover online processing fees, so that my entire contribution goes to \[Masjid Name\] (£X.XX)"

The system calculates Stripe's processing fees (typically 1.5% \+ £0.20 for UK cards) and displays the exact additional amount required. When checked, this fee adds to the donation total, ensuring the full intended donation amount reaches the masjid. Many donors appreciate this option to maximize impact.

**Total Display:**  
 Large text showing final donation amount including any processing fee addition if selected. Updates automatically when fee checkbox toggles. Right-aligned for prominent visibility.

**Payment Method Selection:**

Three buttons provide payment options:

**Apple Pay (Black Button with Apple Logo):**  
 Available only on iOS devices with Apple Pay configured. Tapping opens Apple's native payment sheet with biometric authentication (Face ID or Touch ID). Processes through Stripe's Apple Pay integration.

**PayPal (Button with PayPal Logo):**  
 Redirects to PayPal's authentication interface. Users log into a PayPal account, authorize payment, and return to the app. Processes through Stripe's PayPal integration.

**Pay With Card (White Button):**  
 Opens Stripe's native card entry interface (not a custom screen within the app). Stripe handles all card data collection, validation, and processing, maintaining PCI compliance.

**User Workflow:**

1. **Review Amount:** User sees selected donation amount at top  
2. **Choose Privacy:** Optionally check anonymous donation  
3. **Cover Fees:** Optionally check to add processing fees  
4. **See Total:** Observe final amount including any additions  
5. **Select Payment Method:** Tap preferred payment button  
6. **Process Payment:** Complete payment through selected method's native interface  
7. **Return to App:** Receive success or failure confirmation

**Stripe Integration:**

All payment processing occurs entirely within Stripe's secure infrastructure. The app never sees or stores card numbers, CVV codes, or other sensitive payment data. Stripe returns success/failure status to the app after processing. This architecture maintains PCI DSS compliance without requiring app-level certification.

---

#### **Stripe Payment Processing** {#stripe-payment-processing}

**Payment Method Workflows:**

The application does not implement custom payment entry screens. Instead, it leverages Stripe's native payment interfaces for all payment method handling.

**Process Flow:**

1. **Create Checkout Session:** App sends donation amount, campaign ID, and donor preferences to backend  
2. **Backend Creates Stripe Session:** Backend API calls Stripe to create checkout session with campaign details  
3. **Return Session ID:** Backend returns Stripe session identifier to mobile app  
4. **Launch Stripe UI:** App opens Stripe's native payment sheet using session ID  
5. **User Payment:** User completes payment through Stripe's interface (Apple Pay, Google Pay, card entry, PayPal)  
6. **Stripe Processing:** Stripe handles payment authentication, verification, and processing  
7. **Webhook Notification:** Stripe sends webhook to backend confirming payment success or failure  
8. **Database Update:** Backend updates campaign raised amount and adds donation record  
9. **Return Status:** App receives success/failure result  
10. **Display Confirmation:** App shows success screen or error message

**Stripe Handles:**

* All payment method UI (card forms, Apple Pay sheets, PayPal redirects)  
* PCI compliance and security  
* Payment authentication (3D Secure, biometrics)  
* Fraud detection and prevention  
* Error handling and retry logic  
* Receipt email generation

**App Responsibilities:**

* Creating checkout sessions via backend API  
* Opening Stripe payment interface with session ID  
* Receiving payment completion status  
* Displaying success or error screens  
* Navigating user flow appropriately

#### **Salah Alerts** {#salah-alerts}

**![][image32]**  
 *Description: List of six prayers (Fajr, Sunrise, Zuhr, Asr, Maghrib, Isha), each row showing prayer name with two toggle switches labeled "Alert" and "Athan", all settings independent per prayer*

---

**Alert Configuration Interface:**

Each of the six prayers displays as a row with the prayer name and two toggle switches.

**Toggle Options:**

**Alert Toggle:**  
 Enables or disables notification alert for this specific prayer. When enabled, the device schedules a local notification to fire at the configured time (typically a few minutes before Jamah). Disabled alert means no notification for this prayer.

**Athan Toggle:**  
 Enables or disables audio playback when the alert fires. When enabled and Alert is also enabled, the notification includes adhan sound. When disabled, the notification uses default system sound or silent vibration only.

**Configuration Examples:**

* **Alert ON, Athan ON:** Notification fires with athan audio  
* **Alert ON, Athan OFF:** Notification fires with default sound or vibration  
* **Alert OFF, Athan ON:** No effect (athan requires alert enabled)  
* **Alert OFF, Athan OFF:** No notification

**Independent Prayer Control:**

Each prayer is configured independently. Users might enable Fajr and Maghrib alerts while disabling others based on work schedules. Athan preferences can vary per prayer (e.g., athan for Fajr but silent for Zuhr during work hours).

**Settings Persistence:**

All preferences save locally on the device immediately when toggled. No server synchronization occurs. Settings persist across app restarts. Uninstalling and reinstalling the app resets all alerts to default (typically all disabled).

**Notification Scheduling:**

When users enable alerts, the app schedules local notifications using prayer times from the cached schedule. Notifications reschedule daily to match updated prayer times. The alert timing (how many minutes before Jamah) may be configurable or fixed at a standard value \[TO BE DEFINED in Section 7.3\].

#### **Qibla Direction** {#qibla-direction}

**![][image35]**  
 *Description: Compass interface showing circular dial, cardinal directions (N, S, E, W), rotating compass needle, Kaaba icon indicating Qibla direction, degree display showing bearing to Mecca, "Qibla Direction" label*

**Compass Interface:**

The Qibla compass presents as a circular dial with cardinal direction markers. The interface utilizes device sensors to determine orientation and calculate direction to Mecca.

**Visual Components:**

**Compass Dial:**  
 Circular background with degree markings and cardinal directions (N, S, E, W). The dial may rotate as the device rotates, or remain fixed with the indicator rotating.

**Qibla Indicator:**  
 A distinct marker (often a Kaaba icon or arrow) points toward Mecca's direction. This indicator remains pointed toward Qibla regardless of device orientation.

**Degree Display:**  
 The numeric display shows the bearing to Mecca in degrees (e.g., "287°" or "Southeast"). This provides precise directional information.

**Calibration Notice:**  
 If compass accuracy is low, a message prompts users to calibrate by moving the device in a figure-8 pattern.

**Functionality:**

1. **Permission Request:** First use requests location permission  
2. **Location Acquisition:** App obtains current GPS coordinates  
3. **Calculation:** System calculates great-circle bearing to Mecca (21.4225° N, 39.8262° E)  
4. **Compass Reading:** Device compass provides current heading  
5. **Display Update:** Qibla indicator updates in real-time as device rotates  
6. **Accuracy Indicator:** Visual or textual feedback on accuracy level

**User Experience:**

Users hold the device flat (parallel to ground) for best compass accuracy. Rotating the body while holding the device steady shows Qibla direction remaining constant. When the device aligns with the Qibla indicator pointing forward, users face the correct prayer direction.

**Technical Considerations:**

Compass accuracy depends on device sensors and magnetic interference. Metal structures, electronics, or magnetic objects near devices may affect accuracy. The app may display warnings when accuracy is questionable. Location services must be enabled for calculation.

## **6\. BUSINESS RULES** {#6.-business-rules}

This section defines critical business logic, validation requirements, and system behaviors that govern application functionality.

**Prayer Time Management:**

* Annual CSV uploads overwrite existing prayer times for covered date range  
* Manual edits take precedence over CSV data for specific date ranges  
* Each day must have complete prayer times (all six prayers with Athan and Jamah times, except Sunrise which has Athan only)  
* Jamah time must be after Athan time for each prayer  
* Prayer times cannot be deleted, only modified  
* Islamic date conversion must maintain consistency between admin portal and mobile app displays  
* Friday automatically substitutes Jumu'ah for Zuhr without manual intervention  
* Multiple Jumu'ah times allowed only on Fridays  
* Mobile app caches 30 days of prayer times for offline access  
* Prayer time updates sync to mobile within 60 seconds of admin save

**Event Management:**

* Published events cannot be deleted, only edited or hidden  
* Event end time must be after start time  
* Event images limited to \[MAX\_SIZE\] MB \[TO BE DEFINED\]  
* Supported image formats: JPG, PNG only  
* Events automatically order chronologically in all views  
* Past events remain accessible in admin portal indefinitely  
* Event notifications send only once upon initial publication  
* Re-publishing edited events does not trigger new notifications  
* Draft events invisible to mobile users  
* External registration links must use valid URL format (http:// or https://)

**Announcement Management:**

* Scheduled announcements cannot be scheduled more than 90 days in future  
* Minimum scheduling time: 5 minutes from current time  
* Announcement character limits: Title 100 characters, Message 500 characters  
* Announcements cannot be deleted after sending  
* Failed notification delivery does not prevent announcement from being sent to other users  
* Announcement history persists indefinitely in mobile app

**Campaign Management:**

* Target amount must be positive number greater than zero  
* Campaign end date must be after start date  
* Campaign start date can be today or future date  
* Target amount cannot be modified after first donation received  
* Campaign can be ended manually before end date  
* Ended campaigns cannot be reactivated  
* Campaign progress percentage rounds to nearest whole number  
* Campaigns automatically sort by end date (nearest first) in mobile display  
* Donation amounts must meet minimum threshold of £5  
* Processing fee calculation: 1.5% \+ £0.20 for UK cards \[TO BE CONFIRMED\]  
* Anonymous donations hide donor name from public displays but record internally  
* Campaign images limited to \[MAX\_SIZE\] MB \[TO BE DEFINED\]

**Donation Processing:**

* All payments process through Stripe only  
* Donation receipts sent automatically by Stripe  
* Failed payments do not update campaign totals  
* Payment status updates via webhook within 30 seconds typical  
* Donation history preserves permanently (cannot be deleted by admins)  
* Refunds handled directly through Stripe, not in-app  
* Donation amounts limited to Stripe's transaction limits  
* Currency fixed to GBP for all transactions

**User Access and Authentication:**

* Admin session tokens expire after 24 hours  
* No automatic token refresh mechanism  
* Concurrent admin logins from different devices allowed  
* Account lockout after 5 failed login attempts for 30 minutes  
* Rate limiting: 10 login attempts per 15 minutes per IP  
* Mobile app requires no authentication for any feature  
* User settings persist only on local device  
* No cross-device settings synchronization

**Notification Delivery:**

* Push notifications deliver to devices with app installed and notifications enabled  
* Notification delivery best-effort (no guarantee for offline devices)  
* Notifications appear in notification history even if push delivery fails  
* Each masjid uses unique Firebase topic for message targeting  
* Users auto-subscribe to topic on app installation  
* Prayer alerts use local notifications, not push notifications  
* Local notifications schedule daily based on cached prayer times

**Data Synchronization:**

* Admin actions sync to mobile API within 60 seconds  
* Mobile app checks for updates on app launch  
* Mobile app performs background refresh every 4 hours  
* Pull-to-refresh immediately fetches latest data  
* Offline changes queue and sync when connection restores  
* Conflict resolution favors server data over local cache

**Image and File Handling:**

* All uploaded images stored in AWS S3  
* Image URLs expire after \[DURATION\] requiring regeneration \[TO BE DEFINED\]  
* Supported formats: JPG, PNG for images  
* CSV files must follow exact column structure \[FORMAT TO BE DEFINED\]  
* File upload failures roll back entire operation  
* Corrupted image uploads rejected with error message

**System Behavior:**

* All times display in masjid's configured timezone  
* Date formats follow locale conventions (DD/MM/YYYY for UK)  
* Currency displays as GBP (£) throughout application  
* Empty states display helpful guidance for first-time users  
* Error messages provide actionable guidance, not technical jargon  
* Success confirmations appear briefly (3 seconds) before auto-dismissing  
* Validation occurs both client-side (immediate feedback) and server-side (security)

## **7\. PENDING DECISIONS** {#7.-pending-decisions}

The following items require definition and decision before implementation can be considered complete.

### **7.1 CSV Format Specification** {#7.1-csv-format-specification}

The prayer time CSV upload format requires detailed specification including:

* Exact column names and order  
* Date format (DD/MM/YYYY, MM/DD/YYYY, YYYY-MM-DD)  
* Time format (12-hour with AM/PM, 24-hour)  
* Header row requirement  
* Handling of special characters  
* Sample file for reference

### **7.2 Islamic Calendar Conversion Method** {#7.2-islamic-calendar-conversion-method}

Implementation approach for Gregorian to Islamic date conversion needs definition:

* Pre-computed lookup table  
* Runtime calculation using Hijri library  
* Third-party API integration (e.g., Aladhan API)  
* Accuracy requirements and acceptable variance  
* Handling of different Islamic calendar conventions

### **7.3 Prayer Alert Timing** {#7.3-prayer-alert-timing}

Configuration for when prayer alerts fire requires decision:

* Fixed time before Jamah (e.g., 10 minutes)  
* User-configurable timing  
* Different timing per prayer  
* At Athan time vs. before Jamah time  
* Default setting for new users

### **7.4 Notification Scheduling Mechanism** {#7.4-notification-scheduling-mechanism}

Technical implementation of scheduled announcements needs selection:

* AWS EventBridge scheduled rules  
* Cron jobs on application server  
* Database polling mechanism  
* Third-party scheduling service  
* Reliability and failure handling approach

### **7.5 Campaign Categories** {#7.5-campaign-categories}

Campaign cause categories require finalization:

* Fixed predefined list vs. admin-configurable  
* Complete list of supported categories  
* Category icons and color schemes  
* Multi-category support per campaign  
* Adding new categories post-launch

### **7.6 Campaign End Date Behavior** {#7.6-campaign-end-date-behavior}

System behavior when campaign end date arrives needs specification:

* Automatic campaign closure on end date  
* Manual ending required regardless of date  
* Grace period after end date  
* Notification to admins when end date approaches  
* Handling of donations attempted after end date

### **7.7 Goal Exceeded Handling** {#7.7-goal-exceeded-handling}

Behavior when campaign raises more than target amount requires decision:

* Continue accepting donations after goal reached  
* Automatically close campaign at goal  
* Display "Goal Exceeded" status  
* Set stretch goals or secondary targets  
* Handling of excess funds messaging

### **7.8 Image Upload Specifications** {#7.8-image-upload-specifications}

Complete image upload requirements need definition:

* Maximum file size (suggested: 5MB for events/campaigns, 2MB for logos)  
* Minimum dimensions for quality  
* Automatic resizing or compression  
* Aspect ratio requirements or recommendations  
* Storage duration and cleanup policies

**7.9 Masjid Details Tab Fields**

Complete field list for Masjid Details settings requires specification:

* All required vs. optional fields  
* Field validation rules  
* Character limits per field  
* Services list (fixed vs. custom entry)  
* Facilities list (checkboxes vs. free text)  
* Multiple phone number support  
* Social media links inclusion

### **7.10 Quick Setup Tab Purpose** {#7.10-quick-setup-tab-purpose}

The Quick Setup tab functionality needs complete definition:

* Tab purpose and use case  
* Features included in quick setup  
* Target users (first-time admins vs. all users)  
* Step-by-step wizard or single form  
* Relationship to other settings tabs

### **7.11 Processing Fee Calculation** {#7.11-processing-fee-calculation}

Exact Stripe processing fee structure for UK needs confirmation:

* Standard UK card rate (believed to be 1.5% \+ £0.20)  
* International card rates if different  
* Alternative payment method fees (Apple Pay, PayPal)  
* Currency conversion fees if applicable  
* Fee display rounding rules
